paragraphs.source_en:
After my departure from Pisa, [S.] was magnetised by a lady, which gave rise to the
beautiful stanzas entitled The Magnetic Lady to her Patient, and during which opera-
tion, he made the same reply to an inquiry as to his disease, and its cure, as he had done
to me, — “What would cure me would kill me,” — meaning lithotomy [i.e. surgery to
remove kidney stones].
 (Medwin (1913) 270)
